# GUI Classes

<!-- Generated by tools/guigen.py from sdk/gui/classes.def: don't edit; change the schema and
     run `tools/guigen.py doc sdk/gui/classes.def docs/gui-classes.md`. -->

Every class the GUI service has, as `sdk/gui/classes.def` declares it: the class ABI, appended
only. What the protocol carries and what the classes mean are in
[gui-protocol.md](gui-protocol.md); its §10 says what each class is for.

- **A class has its parents' entries too:** a `Button` is a `Widget`, so it has `enabled`.
- **Abstract** classes can't be made (`Create` answers `BadClass`); their entries are their
  subclasses'.
- **Access:** a property is read (`Get`) and written (`Create`, `Set`), or only one of those.
  An `Atom` property takes only the names listed.
- **Events:** *on* events are sent unless the client turns them off; *off* events only once it
  listens (`Listen`).
- **The C wrappers** (`bmds/guiclasses.h`) are named after these: `bmds_<class>_new`,
  `_set_<property>`, `_get_<property>`, `bmds_<class>_<method>` and
  `BMDS_GUI_<CLASS>_<EVENT>`, in snake case.

## Widget

Abstract.

| Property | Tag | Access | Values |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | Bool | read, written |  |
| `visible` | Bool | read, written |  |
| `stretch` | Int | read, written |  |
| `dropTypes` | List | read, written |  |
| `geometry` | Rect | read only |  |

| Method | Arguments | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `setFocus` | none | none |

| Event | Values | Sent |
|---|---|---|
| `dropped` | String, Bytes, Int, Int | on |
| `contextMenu` | Int, Int | off |
| `wheel` | Int | off |
